integrated_theorem: Conditional theorem with all quantifiers. Fix θ with 0<θ≤1/4. Assume constants Cθ,Kθ≥1 and 0<aθ,cθ≤1, with Cθ≥8Kθ/aθ, have the following RDθ property: for every prime p, every integer 100<d<p, every f:F_p²→F_p, every choice of affine bijections ell_L:F_p→L, and every family P_L∈F_p[t] of degree at most d, write ε=|Eacc|/[p²(p+1)], where Eacc={(ell_L(t),L):P_L(t)=f(ell_L(t))}. If ε≥Cθ(d/p)^(1−θ), then either Agr_d(f)≥cθ ε, or there are an accepted bipartite graph G=(X,T,E)⊆Eacc, a set R⊆T, and an integer D satisfying e(G)≥aθ ε, d≤D≤Kθd, |R|>D, rank Φ_{R,D}<dim V_D, and the following reach condition: every L∈T has more than D distinct incident points x for which some M∈R\{L} is also incident to x in E. Here V_D consists of polynomials of (1,1,d)-weighted degree at most D and Φ_{R,D}(A)=(A(ell_M(t),P_M(t)))_{M∈R}. Under RDθ, there exists one Q∈F_p[X,Y] of total degree at most d with Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]≥cθ* ε, where cθ*=min(cθ,aθ/(2Kθ)). Consequently, if RDθ holds for every 0<θ≤1/4, then for every fixed 0<η<1 there are Cη,cη>0 such that ε≥Cη(d/p)^(1−η) implies one degree-at-most-d Q with agreement at least cη ε.

# Verdict

No unconditional improvement over the cubic benchmark is proved. The strongest integrated result is the exact conditional theorem recorded above: after a bounded-weight rank-or-decode lemma, every algebraic and list-to-one stage closes with only a constant loss. The sole missing obligation is RDθ.

# Coverage receipt

The receipt is frozen at 2026-09-14T10:51:19Z. I inspected TARGET.md, both literature indexes, the 15-file DATA_MANIFEST launch snapshot, all ten submission packages, all ten verifier packages, the four current leaderboards, Lemma Book outputs, corpus-index.json, all completed roadmap rounds and messages, and the campaign databases. The active boards contained 109 bottleneck entries, seven promising submissions, one rejected submission, and two verified submissions. Campaign-300 remained a 301-job queued snapshot with empty boards and no submission or audit output. Every directory named superseded was excluded as instructed. Prompt-only roadmap retries and runtime stderr/cache files contained no completed mathematical claim.

The manifest itself has SHA-256 `343d75e49da76fbab487278e89e8f431ccc37bc29a2da1fafd5d4ba7ef194631`. Eight of its fifteen listed hashes still match. The seven mismatches are precisely the live campaign-10 database, indexes, status, and leaderboards, which changed as ten researchers and ten verifiers completed. This is provenance drift, not missing data.

# Primary-source normalization

For Arora–Sudan, the exact source is the [author's journal manuscript](https://people.csail.mit.edu/madhu/papers/1997/arora-journ.pdf): Lemmas 21–22, Theorem 23, Theorem 34, and Corollary 24. The 1/54 value in the ledger is my solution of the quoted field-size inequality, not a separately stated ratio exponent. :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/.cache/references/arora-sudan.pdf" purpose="source"}

For HKSS, the exact inspected version is [arXiv v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.12752v1): Lemma 3.1, Theorems 4.2–4.4, and Appendix Lemmas B.4 and B.6. The source states the 1/7 weak gate and 1/16 list gate, but the displayed proof's ε³ mass is subsequently treated as ε². The repaired ε⁶ weak output and suggested 1/24 strong threshold are reconstructions, not quoted theorems. :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/.cache/references/hkss.pdf" purpose="source"}

For KTZ, the authoritative source is [ECCC Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download): Theorem 1.1 and Lemmas 2.4–2.7, 3.1–3.2, 4.1–4.3, 5.1–5.2, and 6.1–6.3. The theorem's 1/3 threshold is quoted; the cover/interpolation/root-budget derivation in the ledger is my normalized reconstruction. The cached local copy was used only for navigation because it predates the authoritative revision. :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/.cache/references/ktz.pdf" purpose="source"}

# Integrated conclusion

The corpus points to a sharp separation. Algebraically, D=Oθ(d) is already enough: it makes characteristic problems disappear, makes the O(D/p) cleanup absorbable below ε, and bounds the number of component templates by Oθ(1). The unresolved difficulty is entirely at the incidence handoff: produce such a bounded-weight relation while retaining Ωθ(ε) mass, or recognize and decode the structured table directly. Graph-only covers, uniform multiplicity, bounded-order moments, and the current DRC estimates have all been red-teamed and do not supply that handoff.

proof_steps.proof: This is the only assumed statement. Formal rank deficiency means rank Φ_{R,D}<dim V_D, not merely failure of surjectivity. The graph lies inside Eacc, R⊆T, line parametrizations are affine bijections, and all reached points are distinct.
proof_steps.statement: Assume RDθ with constants Cθ,Kθ,aθ,cθ and Cθ≥8Kθ/aθ.

proof_steps.proof: Put ρ=d/p and x=D/p. From ε≥Cθρ^(1−θ) and D≤Kθd, x≤(Kθ/Cθ)ερ^θ≤aθ ε/8≤1/8. Thus D
proof_steps.statement: Every structured RDθ branch satisfies D

proof_steps.proof: Rank deficiency gives a nonzero A0 in ker Φ. Replace A0 by its squarefree radical A. Every selected-line identity survives because F_p[t] is a domain, and weighted degree does not increase. If A were Z-independent, each of the more than D distinct lines in R would divide a nonzero polynomial of total degree at most D, impossible. Hence A depends on Z. Since deg_Z A<p, A_Z is nonzero.
proof_steps.statement: There is a nonzero squarefree Z-dependent A of weighted degree at most D vanishing formally on every selected graph M∈R.

proof_steps.proof: For a reached point x=ell_L(t)=ell_M(s), acceptedness gives P_L(t)=f(x)=P_M(s). The selected identity on M therefore gives A(x,P_L(t))=0. Each L has more than D distinct such points, while A(ell_L(t),P_L(t)) has degree at most D. Root counting forces the formal identity on L.
proof_steps.statement: A vanishes formally on every line graph indexed by T.

proof_steps.proof: Write A=HB, where H∈F_p[X,Y] is the gcd of the Z-coefficients and B is primitive. Squarefreeness of A makes B squarefree; A_Z=HB_Z≠0 makes B Z-dependent. If H does not vanish identically on L, the identity H|_L·B(ell_L,P_L)=0 cancels in the domain F_p[t]. At most deg H≤D lines are content lines.
proof_steps.statement: Outside at most D content lines, a primitive squarefree Z-dependent B of weighted degree at most D vanishes on every target graph.

proof_steps.proof: If an irreducible C divides both B and B_Z, squarefreeness forces C_Z=0. Since deg_Z C<p, C is Z-independent, contradicting primitivity; hence gcd(B,B_Z)=1. KTZ Lemma 2.6 bounds identically B_Z-ramified graph lines by D(D−1). Including content lines gives fewer than D² bad lines. On every other line, B_Z(ell_L,P_L) is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most D−d≤D. Deleting all nonsimple accepted incidences therefore costs less than (D/p)²+D/p.
proof_steps.statement: Direct vertical cleanup leaves only incidences satisfying B(x,f(x))=0 and B_Z(x,f(x))≠0.

proof_steps.proof: Iteratively delete each current point or line vertex of degree at most D. Every edge is charged once, and the total normalized peeling cost is below 2D/p. Together with P6, total loss is below (D/p)²+3D/p<aθ ε/2. Thus a nonempty graph G1 remains with e(G1)≥aθ ε/2 and minimum degree greater than D.
proof_steps.statement: A clean minimum-degree graph retaining at least half the certificate mass exists.

proof_steps.proof: In a connected component Γ, choose a point b. More than D distinct incident lines pass through the simple root (b,f(b)). The characteristic-free formal implicit recursion, dividing only by B_Z(b,f(b)), gives a unique two-variable branch. Truncate it at total degree d to obtain QΓ. On every incident line this truncation equals P_L, so B(X,Y,QΓ) has total degree at most D and vanishes on more than D distinct lines; hence it is zero. Along an edge, QΓ and P_L are two formal roots with the same simple initial value, so uniqueness makes them identical. Induction through Γ gives QΓ=f on every point vertex. This is the mechanism of KTZ Lemmas 2.5, 2.7, 6.1, and 6.3.
proof_steps.statement: Every connected component Γ of G1 supplies QΓ of total degree at most d with B(X,Y,QΓ)=0 and QΓ=f throughout Γ.

proof_steps.proof: Polynomial division by the monic polynomial Z−QΓ shows that B(X,Y,QΓ)=0 is equivalent to Z−QΓ dividing B. Distinct QΓ give distinct monic irreducible divisors. Consequently the number of distinct component templates is at most deg_Z B≤wdeg(B)/d≤D/d≤Kθ.
proof_steps.statement: All component polynomials form a list of size at most Kθ.

proof_steps.proof: Pigeonhole the edges of G1 by their component template. One Q carries normalized edge mass at least aθ ε/(2Kθ). It equals f on every point incident to those edges. Since each point has at most p+1 incident affine lines, its point agreement is at least the same normalized edge mass.
proof_steps.statement: The structured branch returns one Q with agreement at least aθ ε/(2Kθ).

proof_steps.proof: The direct RDθ branch gives cθ ε; P10 gives aθ ε/(2Kθ) in the structured branch. Taking their minimum proves the claimed fixed-θ conditional theorem.
proof_steps.statement: Under RDθ, agreement is at least min(cθ,aθ/(2Kθ))ε.

proof_steps.proof: For η∈(0,1), take θ=min(η,1/4). Since 0<d/p<1, the η-hypothesis implies the θ-hypothesis. Rename the constants from P11.
proof_steps.statement: Assuming RDθ for every θ∈(0,1/4], the threshold exponent is 1−η for every fixed η∈(0,1).
